title: 영어브리핑_2026-11-16
korean_summary: 오늘 핵심(월): 행거 선적 박스 적입 패킹리스트 함께 확인·인원/시간 수치 받기, 세무서 건 법인장 결정 받기(회신 화요일 정오), 월 결산자료 검토 착수, 화목 주간 보고, 구매 담당 미회신 건 재촉, 토요일 도착 결재·더미 표·보험 재견적 확인.
paragraphs: Good morning, Anthony. Today is Monday, November sixteenth. This is your English briefing for the new week.

On Saturday you had the health check, and you still cleared a lot of mail. So this week starts quite clean. Today we have eight parts. Part one is the top three for today. Part two is reports to collect. Part three is replies you owe. Part four is the schedule and deadlines. Part five is an English review. Part six is a short role-play. Part seven is a practice of key sentences. Part eight is the closing. Let's start.
Part one. The top three for today.
Number one. The garment on hanger box loading is planned for today.

What is it? This is the big buyer shipment on hangers. the export-import leader planned the box loading for November sixteenth. You asked her to use the new way from this shipment. That means you check the first packing list together, and the fixed team gets a short briefing before they start.

Why is it important? Last time, the box sheet had small mistakes, and nobody recorded the number of workers or the time. If we do not record it today, we cannot judge the new price per box. Also, you want to know whether the forwarder will charge the airport security fee again.

Your first action today. Ask the export-import leader what time the loading starts and where. Ask her to send the packing list and the box sheet before it starts. After the loading, ask for three numbers: how many workers, how many hours, and any quantity difference.
Number two. The record from the tax office.

What is it? On Friday afternoon, the chief accountant reported an administrative violation record. It is about some sample invoices that were issued late. The couriers opened export declarations under our tax code, and nobody told the factory. On Saturday morning you replied. You asked her to hold the signing until my director approves it. You also asked four questions.
Why is it important? The penalty itself is small. But once we sign, the record is official. And if more declarations are missing, the same problem will come back at the next refund.

Your first action today. Check that my director has seen your report and ask for his decision. Then remind the chief accountant that items one to three are due by Tuesday noon. Item four belongs to the export-import leader, and it is due on Thursday.
Number three. The monthly closing materials.
What is it? Your calendar shows the monthly closing materials on November fifteenth. That was Sunday, so the work moves to today. The accountant already sent the October income statement last week.

Why is it important? The closing review comes first. After that come the profit and loss report to my director and the file for the head office. If the first step is late, everything after it is late.
Your first action today. Open the October closing files and check that the set is complete. If something is missing, ask the accountant this morning, not this afternoon.
Part two. Reports to collect.

First, the weekly firewood report. Monday is the day for it. You need last week's ledger and the weighing slips. Then you send the weekly report to a head office manager. If the files are not in the folder, you can say this. Could you send me last week's firewood ledger and the weighing slips by ten o'clock?

Second, the data collection for my director. All team leaders had to upload their latest forms to the shared folder by Saturday. Last week, most teams only opened and saved the old files again. Check the folder and the data list this morning. For a team with nothing new, you can say this. The deadline was Saturday, and I do not see any new file from your team. When will you be able to upload it?

Third, the purchasing staff. She is on your watch list, so do not wait. She still owes you the October electricity invoices and the first November bill. She also owes the whiteboard quote and the answer about the sample room air conditioner. Put everything in one message. You can say this. Please send me all four items today. If you cannot, please let me know the reason and the date you can finish.

Fourth, the fabric warehouse leader. Moving the finished styles to the stock rack was due on Saturday. The interlining upload is due this Wednesday. You can say this. Could you let me know where the rack move stands? Please send me the photos today.

Fifth, the attendance staff in the human resources team. Every Monday she corrects last week's absence types in the attendance data. Just check the file. If it is not done by noon, a short reminder is enough.

Sixth, the compliance officer and the IT staff. The hard disk quote for the camera system and the comparison quote for the electrical inspection were both due on Saturday. You can say this. I'm following up on the two quotes that were due on Saturday. Please send what you have today.

Seventh, the trucking price. On Saturday, the export-import leader wrote back to the trucking company. She asked them to follow the same increase and the same start date as other trucking companies. You asked her for a written confirmation that the price will go back when the road ban ends. Check whether the trucking company has answered.
Part three. Replies you owe.

First, the quality manager. On Saturday afternoon he sent the updated dummy list with the yellow cells filled in. You need to review it and decide whether to buy new covers. Your reply can start like this. Thank you for the updated list. I will review it and get back to you on the new covers by Wednesday.

Second, the approvals. Two cash reports arrived on Saturday afternoon. One is the daily cash report, and the other is the weekly cash on hand. Please approve them first thing this morning. No email is needed.

Third, the insurance broker. On Saturday afternoon, the broker sent the renewal quote again with an adjusted insured amount. You already sent the head office the new premium on Saturday morning. So please check that the two files show the same numbers. If they are different, tell the head office manager today. Your reply can start like this. The broker sent a revised quote after my email. Please use the attached file instead.

Fourth, the factory manager. On Saturday you asked him whether we can go ahead with the new sewer grade test. If he says yes, you owe the HR manager the next step. Your message to her can start like this. The factory manager has approved the test. Please start it with the next group of new sewers.

Fifth, a head office manager. You explained how two outside companies really work and asked for his guidance. If his answer comes today, read it carefully before you reply. It is a customs question, so do not answer in a hurry.
Part four. Schedule and deadlines.

Today, Monday. The weekly firewood report. The box loading for the hanger shipment. The monthly closing review. The weekly export and production risk check. And it is a colleague's birthday today, so say happy birthday.
Tuesday, November seventeenth. The tax office answers are due by noon. The short-term workers' pay goes out. It is also the day for the needle order and the weekly consumables report.
Wednesday, November eighteenth. The weekly headcount update and the interlining upload.
Thursday, November nineteenth. The customs declaration check is due. The new quote for fire system maintenance is also due.
Friday, November twentieth. At nine o'clock, check whether the forwarder charged the security fee for today's shipment. It is also the day to check the export and import cost ledger.
One more date. The current collective labor agreement ends on November twenty-fourth. That is next Tuesday. Please ask the HR manager where the registration stands.
Part five. English review.
We will review eight expressions from your recent cards. Listen, and then say each one out loud.

Number one. The expression is, finalize. It means to finish something and make it final. For example, we need to finalize the closing file before we send it to the head office. Now say it with me. We need to finalize the closing file.
One more time. We need to finalize the closing file.

Number two. The expression is, expedite. It means to make something happen faster. For example, could you expedite the two quotes? They were due on Saturday. Now say it with me. Could you expedite the two quotes?
One more time. Could you expedite the two quotes?

Number three. The expression is, we'd like to go ahead with something, provided that something is true. It means we will do it, but only on one condition. For example, we'd like to go ahead with the new test, provided that the line leaders agree. Now say it with me. We'd like to go ahead with the new test, provided that the line leaders agree.
One more time. We'd like to go ahead with the new test, provided that the line leaders agree.

Number four. The expression is, unless I hear otherwise by a certain time, I will do something. It means I will act if nobody stops me. For example, unless I hear otherwise by noon, I will send the report to the head office. Now say it with me. Unless I hear otherwise by noon, I will send the report.
One more time. Unless I hear otherwise by noon, I will send the report.

Number five. The expression is, it has been some time since something, and something still has not happened. It is a polite way to push. For example, it has been two days since the deadline, and the files still have not been uploaded. Now say it with me. It has been two days since the deadline, and the files still have not been uploaded.
One more time. It has been two days since the deadline, and the files still have not been uploaded.

Number six. The expression is, revert. It means to go back to the way it was before. For example, will the trucking company revert to the old price when the road ban ends? Now say it with me. Will they revert to the old price when the ban ends?
One more time. Will they revert to the old price when the ban ends?

Number seven. The expression is, going forward, please do something. It means from now on. For example, going forward, please give the two documents to the export staff on the shipping day. Now say it with me. Going forward, please give the two documents to the export staff on the shipping day.
One more time. Going forward, please give the two documents to the export staff on the shipping day.

Number eight. The expression is, it turned out that something was true. You use it when you find the real reason later. For example, it turned out that the couriers opened the declarations without telling us. Now say it with me. It turned out that the couriers opened the declarations without telling us.
One more time. It turned out that the couriers opened the declarations without telling us.
Good. Try to use one of these in a real email today.
Part six. Role-play.
This morning you will talk to my director about the tax office record. Listen to the conversation first.
Anthony says. Good morning, my director. Do you have two minutes? It is about the record from the tax office.
My director says. Yes, I saw your message. What happened exactly?
Anthony says. The sales team sent samples by courier. The couriers opened export declarations under our tax code, but they did not inform the factory. So we issued the invoices late.
My director says. How did the tax office find it?
Anthony says. They found it during the refund review in April. It turned out that some declarations were missing from our records. We issued all the invoices as soon as we found out.
My director says. Is there any tax impact?
Anthony says. No. They are free samples, so the invoice value is zero. There is only a small administrative penalty.
My director says. Then why don't we just sign it and close it?
Anthony says. Before we sign, I'd like to check two things. First, how the penalty was calculated. Second, whether more declarations are missing. The chief accountant will answer by Tuesday noon.
My director says. And how do we stop it from happening again?
Anthony says. Going forward, I will ask the sales team to tell our export-import team before they send any sample by courier. I will also ask the couriers not to use our tax code without notice.
My director says. Okay. Report to me again on Tuesday afternoon.
Anthony says. Yes. Unless I hear otherwise, we will hold the signing until then.
That is the end of the conversation. Now repeat two key sentences.
Sentence one. Before we sign, I'd like to check two things.
One more time. Before we sign, I'd like to check two things.
Sentence two. Unless I hear otherwise, we will hold the signing until then.
One more time. Unless I hear otherwise, we will hold the signing until then.
Part seven. Practice of key sentences.
These are four sentences you can really use today. Say each one after me.
Sentence one, for the export-import leader. What time does the box loading start today, and where?
Sentence two, also for the export-import leader. After the loading, please tell me the number of workers and the hours.
Sentence three, for the purchasing staff. Please send me all four items today.
Sentence four, for the quality manager. I will get back to you on the new covers by Wednesday.
Well done.
Part eight. Closing.

Let me say the most important thing one more time. Today, join the box loading from the first packing list, and get the numbers after it. Get my director's decision on the tax office record. And start the monthly closing review this morning.
Three things, in that order. The rest can wait until the afternoon.
Have a good Monday, Anthony. See you tomorrow.
